subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@fintechco.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap and the info we need to size Dedicated for FinTechCo so we can get a formal proposal over to procurement. Attached: dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx (a simple worksheet to capture traffic patterns).

Call recap (TL;DR):
- Use case: real-time payment assistance + fraud explanation generation (low latency requirement for the UX).
- Planned go-live: Q4 2026 (pilot in mid-Oct).
- Data residency: US only; no on-prem required today but might revisit for regulated flows in 2027.

Sizing questions / asks (can you reply inline?):
1) Target sustained TPS for text-generation endpoints (not embeddings) during business hours and peak (e.g., 100 TPS sustained, 300 TPS peak).
2) Typical prompt + response token mix (avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens) — if you can drop a sample CSV (token-sample.csv) that'd be ideal.
3) Concurrency requirement per user session (how many parallel requests per host/session).
4) Any preferred GPU family for Dedicated (we typically recommend A10G or H100 depending on throughput and cost goals).
5) Procurement timelines / approvals we should be aware of (SOW, PoA, required security docs).

Proposed next steps:
- You fill the sizing sheet + token sample and reply (we'll use that to model TPS -> GPU mapping).
- I’ll draft a capacity proposal (expected GPUs, concurrency, burst policy) and send a preliminary cost estimate to route to procurement.
- Rafael (cc’d) will join the pricing/discount conversation.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if easier.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx

From: Sara Khan <sara@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom@fintechco.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the sizing sheet. Quick answers inline below and attached a sample token export (token-sample.csv) from our staging traffic.

1) TPS: During business hours we see ~60 TPS sustained across our feature surface today; expected growth to 180 TPS sustained within 3 months after pilot. Peak spikes up to ~450 TPS for short bursts (1-2 minutes) during load tests.
2) Token mix: average prompt ~120 tokens, average response ~350 tokens (see token-sample.csv).
3) Concurrency per user: most user flows make a single request, but some batch flows (report generation) send 6 parallel requests; we estimate 2.5 average concurrency for active sessions.
4) GPU preference: no hard constraint — cost is a factor; if Redwood can show H100s materially improve lat/lower cost per token we’d consider them, otherwise A10G to start.
5) Procurement: procurement team needs a high-level SOW, SOC2 and encryption details, and an estimated monthly cost to start a procurement ticket. They typically take 3–4 weeks for standard SaaS SOW.

Also copied Tom (engineering) who asked for an initial map from TPS -> GPU counts and any latency estimates for 350-token responses.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Product | FinTechCo
sara@fintechco.com

Attachment: token-sample.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@fintechco.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the token sample — super helpful. Based on your numbers (60 -> 180 sustained, 450 peak, avg response 350 tokens) here are preliminary recommendations and assumptions: 

Assumptions:
- Model: we modeled on an LLM similar in size to a 33B/70B family (optimized quantized variant).
- Average generation time scaled for 350-token responses.
- Continuous batching and KV caching used where possible; prefix caching for repeated system prompts.

Preliminary sizing (sustained vs peak):
- Starting pilot (180 TPS sustained target): recommend a Dedicated pool of 6 x A10G (initial) to meet latency SLO (~150–250ms per token median) with concurrency tuning (approx 6–8 concurrent in-flight requests per GPU).
- Peak burst handling (450 TPS short bursts): enable burst capacity to an additional 6 A10G-equivalent GPUs (burst pool) or use regional fallback to hosted capacity for short spikes.
- If you want to optimize for unit-cost at scale and tolerate slightly higher per-request latency variability, H100 option: 2–3 x H100 nodes could replace the 6 A10G footprint for sustained throughput depending on model optimization — H100 favors throughput but costs more per GPU-hour. We’ll include both cost profiles in the proposal.

Concurrency & policy suggestions:
- Set default request concurrency per session to 2 and a max per API key of 50 concurrent requests to protect the pool.
- Configure autoscaling with a conservative ramp (scale at 70% CPU/KV cache utilization) and configure burst to be available for short windows (1–5 minutes).

Deliverables from us this week:
- Preliminary capacity proposal + cost estimate (Redwood-Proposal-FinTechCo-v1.pdf).
- Short SOW template and SOC2 summary to hand to procurement.

Next steps:
1) I’ll attach the proposal and SOW. Rafael, can you draft an initial pricing/discount note we should include for procurement?
2) Sara/Tom — if you confirm pilot target (180 TPS sustained) and timeline (mid-Oct pilot), we’ll finalize and send the formal proposal for procurement review.

Happy to hop on 30 mins tomorrow to walk through the proposal if that’s helpful.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-FinTechCo-v1.pdf

Looping in here with pricing guidance — I’ll prepare the detailed pricing sheet but high-level notes:
- For the pilot (6 A10G + burst policy), list price is $X/month; we can offer a 15% pilot discount with commitment to a 6-month reserved window.
- H100 option will show higher list but lower GPU count; include both options side-by-side in the proposal so procurement can compare TCO.
- Include an enterprise add-on for extended observability (Redwood Console retention + tracing) — procurement often asks for it; price as an optional line item.

Internal next steps for us:
- Rafael: produce pricing and discount scenarios by EOD.
- Aditya: validate that autoscaling/burst behavior is feasible for the suggested config and add a short note on expected median latencies for the 350-token responses on both A10G and H100 configs.
- Marissa: follow up with Sara to confirm pilot TPS target and procurement timeline; once confirmed we send formal proposal + SOW to procurement.

Rafael
